blocks.text: 以下是我们当天最重要的几点收获：

inlines.text: 以下是我们当天最重要的几点收获：
如今智能体编程已证明其非凡价值，业内许多公司都在专注于降低成本。在短暂盛行的“堆 token”风潮之后，构成 AI 行业大部分收入的企业计算客户正意识到，成本可能很快就会变得非常高昂。专用芯片、开源大语言模型以及各种优化策略都在被采用。
围绕开源大语言模型的争论正变得更加激烈。行业内部出现了真正的分歧：一方认为智能最终将成为一种商品，主要由开源模型驱动；另一方则认为前沿实验室能够保持决定性优势。
初创公司担心未来 Anthropic、OpenAI 和大型科技巨头会有效控制对前沿智能的访问。
眼下所有热度都集中在基础设施上，背后的基本假设是终端需求在可预见的未来会持续纵向增长。然而在 CVAI 上，关于应用的讨论却出奇地少。编程是一个杀手级应用，但再往后就说不清了。Perplexity CEO
表示：“不可能所有人都在建基础设施，那样就只剩基础设施、没有需求了。你需要真正世界级的应用。”
会上也隐约流露出对公众敌视 AI 的担忧。General Catalyst 的 Taneja 指出，“资本主义是一种特权”，是社会授予的，交换条件是改善人们的生活；而 AI 除了让企业 IT 更高效、更有成效之外，还需要切实证明自己到底好在哪。
在我们的现场投票中，八成与会者认为我们正处在泡沫之中，不过多数人认为这是明年或更往后才会爆发的问题。

blocks.text: 以下是我们最喜欢的一些发言：

inlines.text: 以下是我们最喜欢的一些发言：
“我们必须打造出足够多的千亿美元公司，才能确保创新在规模化层面继续发挥作用。”——General Catalyst 的
“对世界最有利、对美国最有利的，是 AI 的去中心化，而不是把所有一切都集中到某一种模型选项上。”——Vercel 的
“全球 GDP 大约 115 万亿美元，其中约 65 万亿是劳动力。AI 是第一个能承担其中一部分工作的技术……AI 不必取代劳动力，只要从中分到一小片，就是一笔大数目。”——Bessemer Venture Partners 的
“（Crosby 招的）每一个人都必须头脑灵活，并且能坦然接受这样一个事实：每隔几个月，你以前做过的事，电脑就能做了。”——Crosby 的
“人们越来越意识到，AI 与其说是网络效应型产品，不如说是深度递归型产品。真正重度使用它的人只是少数。大约 80% 的收入来自 20% 的用户。这里存在一个关键的幂律。”——Perplexity 的
“一边是大型 AI 公司，它们觉得自己有责任充当 AI 系统的控制者和所有者……另一边，我们主张 AI 应当更加民主化。世界上任何公司都应该拥有可以引入内部的自己的 AI 模型。”——River AI 的

There was a fascinating split-screen at CVAI as attendees reckoned with the salacious news even as they marveled at the AI opportunities ahead.

blocks.text: Earlier in the day, Shaun Maguire floated Palo Alto Networks CEO Nikesh Arora as a candidate to run Nvidia. On stage, Arora deflected on whether he’d take the role but agreed Huang’s departure was likely to bring some short-term instability. Executives with especially close ties to Huang, including Flapping Airplanes president Asher Spector and Perplexity CEO Aravind Srinivas, sidestepped questions about what it might mean for their companies; Huang has personally led the company’s controversial strategy of investing in its customers, and that’s likely to be reined in by interim CEO Colette Kress.

blocks.text: Still, for all the potential dislocations of the Nvidia crisis, AI progress keeps accelerating, numerous speakers noted. Demand for compute remains off the charts. Tech stocks coughed on the Nvidia news, but by week’s end had largely stabilized. The city of San Francisco is buzzing like it hasn’t been in a long time: we’ve spent a lot of time downtown over the past five years, and Thursday was the first time that it felt to us like the city was really, truly back.

blocks.text: Here are a few of our biggest takeaways from the day:

inlines.text: Here are a few of our biggest takeaways from the day:

Now that agentic coding has proven its extraordinary value, a lot of the industry is focused on bringing down costs. After the brief heyday of token-maxing, the enterprise computing customers who make up the bulk of AI industry revenues are realizing that it can get very expensive, very fast. Purpose-built chips, open source LLMs, and a variety of optimization strategies are all in play.

The debate over open source LLMs is getting even more heated. There’s a real split in the industry between those who believe that intelligence will ultimately be a commodity, heavily powered by open source models, and those who believe that the frontier labs can maintain a decisive edge.
Startups are worried about a future where Anthropic, OpenAI, and the Big Tech incumbents effectively control access to cutting-edge intelligence.

All of the heat right now is around infrastructure, grounded in a baseline assumption that end-demand will grow vertically for the foreseeable future. Yet there was surprisingly little discussion of applications at CVAI. Coding is a killer app, but after that it gets fuzzy. “Everybody can’t be building infra, then you have only infra, without demand,” said Perplexity CEO

There were hints of concern about public hostility to AI. Taneja of General Catalyst observed that “capitalism is a privilege,” one that’s granted by society in exchange for improving lives, and AI still needs to show exactly what it’s good for, beyond making corporate IT more efficient and effective.
Eighty percent of attendees said in our live poll that we’re in a bubble, though a majority thought it was a problem for next year, or beyond.

blocks.text: Here are some of our favorite quotes:

inlines.text: Here are some of our favorite quotes:
“We have to build enough $100 billion companies to make sure innovation continues to have a role at scale.” —
“What’s best for the world and what’s best for America is the decentralization of AI as opposed to total concentration in one model option.” —

“Global GDP is about $115 trillion, and about $65 trillion of that is labor. AI is the very first technology that does some of that work… AI doesn’t have to replace the workforce, it just needs to capture a small sliver of it to make that number.” —
“Every single person [hired by Crosby] has to have a pliable mind and be comfortable with the fact that every few months, what you have done before, a computer can do.” —

“People are increasingly realizing that AI is a deeply recursive product more than a network-effect product. There are a few people who use it a lot. 80% of the revenue is probably coming from 20% of the users. There’s a key power law there.” —

“On one side, we’ve got the large AI companies. They feel like it’s their responsibility to be the controllers and the owners of the AI systems… On the other hand, we have the idea [that] AI should be more democratized. Any company in the world should have their own AI models that they can bring in-house.” —
